item.title: Should GTA 6 have been nominated at The Game Awards? Have your say!
item.dc:content:
GTA 6 led the nominations at The Game Awards - but should it even have been eligible in the first place? Rockstar's latest seems a likely candidate to dominate the entire awards season, but opinions on its validity for The Game Awards 2026 seem to vary significantly, so we want to know what you think of this year's frontrunner.

The short version: the nominees for The Game Awards 2026 were announced yesterday, November 17 - two full days before GTA 6 would actually be available for the vast majority of players. Yet despite not having been publicly released, Rockstar's was the most-nominated game of the show, picking up a total of eight nods, with the option for the public to cast their votes on a game that hadn't even been reviewed yet. The response was...confused, to say the least.

Those defending the nominations have a few points in their favor. Possibly the most obvious is the fact that by the time The Game Awards roll around next month, GTA 6 will have spent a few weeks in players' hands. Arguably even more compelling is that The Game Awards are primarily a jury-selected affair, meaning a panel of experts from around the industry - many of whom will have had early access for their GTA 6 review - will have been partly responsible for picking the nominees. Given the glowing reviews that the game's received today, it's safe to say those people think GTA 6 is in GOTY territory.

But on the other hand, public voting does account for some of The Game Awards' selection process. Most people throwing out a vote for GTA 6 in the hours after the nominations were announced would have been doing so before review scores were even unveiled, let alone before getting their own hands on the game. Many others are unlikely to experience the game in full by the time of the awards - unless you're mainlining it over the next couple of weeks, you probably won't have rolled credits without some serious dedication.

Those are the facts of the matter, but what do you think? GTA 6 is pretty much guaranteed to be a mainstay of the awards circuit for the next 12 months, but this is a slightly wonky foot to start that journey off on. You can cast your own vote in the poll at the top of this article, or let us know exactly what your take is in the comments section below.

Why wasn't GTA 6 at the Golden Joystick Awards?

item.title: GTA 6 Bigfoot sightings already ramping up as Rockstar honors a 22-year-old Grand Theft Auto legend
item.dc:content:
GTA 6 is now slowly rolling out across the world – or not so slowly, if you use the New Zealand trick – and players are already starting to uncover the game's secrets. I'd give you a spoiler warning here, but you should probably already be on internet blackout if you're concerned about seeing little surprises early. After all, multiple people have already discovered Bigfoot.

It seems that Bigfoot's appearance is tied to a single location in the game, as every player I've come across – whether the clip is on YouTube, Twitter, Reddit, or Instagram – finds him feasting on a bloody deer corpse at a dirt road intersection. If you chase Bigfoot into the woods, you'll likely stumble upon a strange effigy of a person tied to a tree. If you investigate it, you'll soon fall over, see Bigfoot approach as you lose consciousness, and awaken back where you first saw the creature.

Bigfoot's got a long history in GTA, going back to the PS2 era. He didn't actually appear in San Andreas, but rumors about his presence there became so prolific that Rockstar would eventually reference them in other games, and he's had some pretty extensive cameos in GTA 5 and GTA Online.

This appearance in GTA 6 seems a lot less mysterious, given its singular location and how many people have already stumbled on it. But GTA 5's Easter eggs got pretty involved, and I wouldn't be at all surprised if it's just the first step in a wider cryptid mystery. I still need to know if the UFO is going to make a comeback…

If you're just getting started, check out our guide to all the pre-order and Ultimate Edition bonuses in GTA 6

item.title: GTA 6 devs react to unprecedented reviews: "I feel like a kid on Christmas morning"
item.dc:content:
Miraculously, Rockstar has met the moment with GTA 6. Years of anticipation, an unparalleled budget, and unprecedented hype have culminated in a reception unlike anything I've seen in my 10 years writing about video games. GTA 6 is a bona fide masterpiece, according to pretty much every review out there, boasting an earth-shattering 99 Metascore, tying with 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for highest rated game of all time despite having far more reviews factored in. It's a great day for Rockstar fans, but it's an even better day for the developers who worked on the game and get to experience such a momentous payoff.

"Having a proper moment at the launch and the reviews coming in," writes associate lead programmer Allan Walton on Twitter. "So happy it’s finally out and it’s been received so well. Congrats to the team who’ve worked so hard for this."

"From us to you. Truly grateful to be a part of this masterpiece. Still feels surreal!" says Rockstar production coordinator Navya Manaswitha.

"HOLY... I don't know what to say, after working on this game for almost 8 years, I'm so proud of what we all accomplished together, I feel like a kid on Christmas morning! I hope you all enjoy!" reads a post from senior environment artist Jonathon Gregory Bick.

"Today's been fucking mental. Best team in the world. Hope y'all have the best time in Leonida!!" reads a reaction from a senior QA tester going by Jodie on Twitter.

Here are some less wordy, but equally expressive, reactions to GTA 6's phenomenal reviews:

GamesRadar+'s GTA 6 review echoes many others in calling Rockstar's latest a generational achievement on every level. "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation," writes GR+ editor-in-chief Josh West. "Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments."

The games industry is in a pretty messy place right now with ongoing layoffs, difficult AI conversations, and exorbitant hardware prices, but the joy around GTA 6 is infectious today. Very few games, if any, rival GTA when it comes to unifying the audience in jubilant celebration amid so much turbulence, and I'm just grateful to be taking part. Now, it's just a test of patience as people from various time zones await the GTA 6 release time in their region.

As GTA 6 finally releases, Rockstar boss Sam Houser issues rare statement – "We are incredibly grateful" and "look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you"
